tool.name: Carat balance
tool.measures: the weight of the stone, in carats or in grams
tool.where: Gemmology House and Office, bottom row, in the middle of the laboratory
tips: Switch the balance on (ON/OFF) before putting the stone on it

steps.title: The carat
steps.text:
Stones are weighed in carats. One carat is 0.2 gram.

The word comes from the carob seed, which merchants used long ago as a weight: all the seeds weigh almost the same.

steps.title: Weighing a stone
steps.text:
1. Switch on the balance with the ON/OFF button.
2. Put the stone on the pan.
3. Wait until the display is steady, then read the weight.

The balance gives hundredths of a carat: a 2.35 ct stone weighs 0.470 g.

steps.title: Carats or grams
steps.text:
A button changes the display unit. Remember the conversion: 1 g = 5 ct.

We speak in carats for stones, in grams for rough crystals and heavier objects.

steps.title: Weight is not size
steps.text:
Two stones of the same size do not weigh the same: it all depends on the density of the material. A ruby is heavier than a quartz of the same volume.

Note this weight well: it is also used to work out density, with the hydrostatic balance.
